about.title: Arcata Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Arcata's compact street grid puts a lot of local traffic onto a handful of corridors — Samoa Boulevard, Alliance Road, 11th Street, and H Street among them. Public records show 37 injury collisions and 40 injured people in the most recent full year, with a concentration of reports on Friday nights between midnight and 2 a.m. Whether your crash happened near the Plaza, on the way to Cal Poly Humboldt, or out toward the edge of town, the aftermath tends to look similar: medical visits, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a statement before you've even seen a doctor. Our team handles car accident claims in Arcata and can review what happened, explain your options, and take on the insurance conversations while you focus on healing. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or transit vehicle — was involved. We can flag that deadline early so it doesn't quietly pass you by.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but any percentage assigned to you reduces what you can recover. Insurers know this, which is why an early recorded statement — before you understand the full picture — can be used to shift blame your way.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but that doesn't mean an insurer will offer it freely. We work on contingency only, so there's no upfront cost to having someone push back on your behalf.

items.question: I was in a crash near 11th Street and the insurance adjuster already called. Should I give a statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can talk to them on your behalf so you're not navigating that alone.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a road maintained by the city or county?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California often carry a much shorter deadline — sometimes as little as six months instead of the usual two years. If your crash involved a city vehicle, transit bus, or a road maintenance issue in Arcata, it's worth getting a quick attorney review sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does your firm charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. There's no cost for an initial consultation with our team. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
